scope.when_absent: this corpus records no scope notes (no commit carries Applies:); the absence is not a statement that the change reaches every case

default_reach.rule: presumption against retrospectivity; immediate application to procedure
default_reach.meaning: an enactment is presumed not to apply to facts completed before it came into force, or to interfere with vested rights, unless Parliament says so expressly or by necessary implication; procedural provisions apply immediately to pending matters; a repeal does not affect rights acquired or proceedings begun under the repealed enactment; in criminal law, no one may be found guilty of an act that was not an offence when committed, and a person found guilty is entitled to the lesser punishment where it was varied between the offence and sentencing
default_reach.authority: Interpretation Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. I-21, s. 43 (effect of repeal) and s. 44 (repeal and substitution); Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 11(g) and 11(i); R. v. Dineley, 2012 SCC 58, [2012] 3 S.C.R. 272; Tran v. Canada (Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness), 2017 SCC 50, [2017] 2 S.C.R. 289
